The Contracting Officer may at any time, by written order, and without notice to the sureties, if any, make changes within the general scope of this contract in any one or more of the following: a. Method of shipment or packing. b. Place of delivery. c. Time of delivery. If any such change causes an increase or decrease in the cost of, or the time required for, performance of any part of the work under this contract, whether or not changed by the order, the Contracting Officer shall make an equitable adjustment in the contract price, the delivery schedule, or both, and shall modify the contract, unless the contract terms provide for regional delivery pricing that covers cost adjustments. The Contractor must assert its right to an adjustment under this clause within 30 days from the date of receipt of the written order. However, if the Contracting Officer decides that the facts justify it, the Contracting Officer may receive and act upon a proposal submitted before final payment of the contract. If the Contractor’s proposal includes the cost of property made obsolete or excess by the change, the Contracting Officer shall have the right to prescribe the manner of the disposition of the property. Failure to agree to any adjustment shall be a dispute under the Disputes clause. However, nothing in this clause shall excuse the Contractor from proceeding with the contract as changed. award_criteria.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment_1_-_On_Off_Ramping_Procedures.docx ===== ON AND OFF RAMP PROCEDURES On-Ramping: The Government reserves the right to expand the competitive pool for small business competition at any time during the term of the contract. The Government will advertise the re-opening of the competition on SAM.gov. The evaluation and selection of awardees for any on-ramp will be exactly the same as the evaluation and award criteria used for the MACC initial basic contract awards. Any additions due to on-ramps will not impact the MACC ceiling. The Government anticipates the following awards: Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Awards – The Government intends to make eight (8) awards to the firms comprising the HTROs. The Government anticipates maintaining similar numbers of contracts awarded under each scope throughout the duration of the period of performance but may choose to have more or fewer contracts depending on the availability of qualified offerors and the needs of the Government. Successful on-ramp awardees will compete with any existing or remaining contractors

Hotlist The contractor will compile a Trouble Ticket Hotlist up to three times per five-day work week on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, at the discretion of the 21 CS/CC. These Hotlists shall be sent to all 21 CS Flight Leads and Senior Leadership. This notification email will include all pertinent data on all currently open High Priority tickets and information on any other applicable high visibility projects or concerns. Hands on training from CFP technicians concerning the exact process used to present the relevant Hotlist data will be provided from current CFP government employees during the 90-day military-to- contractor turnover period. Compilation of Ticket Data The contractor will perform a once-weekly task known as “Running the Numbers”, an action performed on both NIPRNET and SIPRNET using Remedy which exports data into Microsoft Excel. This process generates charts and metrics which are then sent to leaders once per week for the purpose of overall ticket status and numbers awareness, and to perform Trend Analysis. If a leader can see a negative trend, this allows them to intervene to reprioritize work, expand office hours or take other actions in the interest of increased productivity.
